subject: angol
title: Thirty days, ten thousand steps
instructions: Read the article from a school magazine about a walking challenge and answer the questions (1–8). Use no more than FOUR words for each answer. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Olvasd el az iskolaújság cikkét egy gyaloglós kihívásról, és válaszolj a kérdésekre (1–8). Egy válasz legfeljebb NÉGY szó lehet. A 0. a példa.

passage.title: Thirty days, ten thousand steps
passage.subtitle: Class 11B tried a month-long walking challenge. Here is what happened.

blocks.text: It all started in a biology lesson in October. Our teacher, Mr Horváth, told us that many teenagers walk only about 5,000 steps a day, and that most of us spend more than eight hours a day sitting down. Then he made a suggestion: for thirty days, all 26 of us would try to walk at least 10,000 steps every day. We would count our steps with our phones and share the numbers in a class chat group.

The first week was the hardest. On the first day, only nine of us reached 10,000 steps. Most of us were surprised by how little we normally moved. 'I thought I was quite active,' said Bori, 'but on a normal school day I only walked about 3,000 steps – mostly between my bed, the bus stop and the school canteen.'

We soon found ways to walk more. Several students started getting off the bus two stops early and walking the rest of the way to school. Others took the stairs instead of the lift in the shopping centre, or walked their dogs for longer. Dani, who had never walked anywhere if he could avoid it, began going to football training on foot – a 40-minute walk.

By the third week, almost everyone was reaching the goal on most days. Many of us noticed changes. Several students said they slept better, and a few said they felt less stressed before tests. Lucas, an exchange student from Germany, said the best part was that he discovered parts of the city he had never seen before.

Not everything was positive, though. On rainy days it was difficult to find the motivation to go out, and some people felt that the competition in the chat group became too serious. One student even admitted that she had shaken her phone to get more steps!

At the end of the month, 21 of the 26 students had walked at least 10,000 steps on more than 25 days. Mr Horváth was so pleased that he has suggested a new challenge for the spring: a whole month without using lifts or escalators.

example.prompt: In which lesson did the idea for the challenge come up?
example.explanation: Az egész egy biológiaórán kezdődött októberben: „in a biology lesson”.
example.evidence: It all started in a biology lesson in October.

items.prompt: According to Mr Horváth, how many steps do many teenagers walk a day?
items.explanation: A tanár szerint sok kamasz naponta csak körülbelül 5000 lépést tesz meg („only about 5,000 steps a day”). A 10 000 a kitűzött cél, nem ez a válasz.
items.evidence: many teenagers walk only about 5,000 steps a day

items.prompt: What did the students use to count their steps?
items.explanation: A lépéseiket a telefonjukkal számolták: „with our phones”.
items.evidence: We would count our steps with our phones

items.prompt: How many students reached 10,000 steps on the first day?
items.explanation: Az első napon csak kilencen érték el a 10 000 lépést („only nine of us”). A 26 az osztály létszáma, a 21 pedig a hónap végi eredmény.
items.evidence: On the first day, only nine of us reached 10,000 steps.

items.prompt: What did some students use instead of the lift in the shopping centre?
items.explanation: Néhányan a bevásárlóközpontban a lift helyett a lépcsőt (the stairs) használták.
items.evidence: Others took the stairs instead of the lift in the shopping centre

items.prompt: How did Dani start getting to football training?
items.explanation: Dani, aki addig sehova nem ment gyalog, elkezdett gyalog (on foot) járni a focira – ez 40 perces séta.
items.evidence: began going to football training on foot

items.prompt: Apart from sleeping better, what change did a few students notice before tests?
items.explanation: Néhányan azt mondták, hogy dolgozatok előtt kevésbé voltak stresszesek („felt less stressed”). Ugyanezt jelentő válasz (pl. less nervous, more relaxed) is elfogadható.
items.evidence: a few said they felt less stressed before tests

items.prompt: What sometimes made it difficult to find the motivation to go out?
items.explanation: Esős napokon (on rainy days) nehéz volt rávenni magukat, hogy kimenjenek. A chatcsoportbeli verseny egy másik probléma volt, az nem a kimenést nehezítette.
items.evidence: On rainy days it was difficult to find the motivation to go out

items.prompt: What did one student do to get more steps?
items.explanation: Az egyik diák bevallotta, hogy megrázta a telefonját (shook her phone), hogy több lépést mutasson – vagyis csalt.
items.evidence: she had shaken her phone to get more steps
